themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints in CD 318 surged to 10 THIS WEEK, up 7900% from a baseline of 0.1 complaints per week over the prior 8 weeks, signaling either a rapid enforcement gap, coordinated poster activity, or emerging code violation campaign affecting neighborhood visibility and aesthetics.
evidence: 10 illegal posting complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 29.86)
7900% spike represents most statistically extreme deviation in entire complaint dataset
Represents sudden emergence, not gradual drift—suggests triggering event or infrastructure failure
reporting_angles: Ground canvassing: Where is posting concentrated? (subway, commercial strips, residential)—any pattern?
311 deep-dive: Are complaints from same reporter or spread across district? What are posts advertising?
Sanitation response: Is DSNY enforcement lagging, or is volume genuinely new?

themes_detail.label: Street Noise Spike This Week
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints jumped to 19 THIS WEEK, a 300% increase from the 4.8-complaint weekly baseline (z-score: 2.72), indicating a new source of sustained noise disturbance—possibly construction, street vendors, or event activity.
evidence: 19 noise–street/sidewalk complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.8 weekly average baseline (300% increase, z-score: 2.72)
Distinct from vehicle noise spike (separate category, last week, 231% up)
Suggests location-specific, non-vehicular source rather than general ambient noise
reporting_angles: Geomapping: Which blocks/intersections are generating complaints? Canvass them for construction, street fairs, bars, vendor clusters.
Timeline: Did spike align with weekend, holiday, or specific event?
Resident interviews: What type of noise (music, shouting, equipment)? Time of day? Duration?

themes_detail.label: Vehicle Noise Disturbance
themes_detail.summary: Vehicle noise complaints climbed to 12 LAST WEEK, up 231% from a 3.6-complaint weekly baseline (z-score: 3.66), likely linked to modified exhaust systems, drag racing, or event-related traffic in Flatlands/Canarsie corridors.
evidence: 12 noise–vehicle complaints LAST WEEK vs. 3.6 weekly average (231% increase, z-score: 3.66)
Distinct spike from street/sidewalk noise, suggesting vehicular source rather than construction/events
Canarsie corridor known for car culture; spike may reflect organized activity (car meets, racing)
reporting_angles: NYPD records: Are there reports of illegal street racing, burnouts, or organized car meetups in district?
Community intel: Talk to residents on major thoroughfares (Flatbush Ave, Nostrand Ave, Jamaica Bay routes) about timing and type of noise.
Enforcement gap: Is NYPD responding to 311 noise complaints at typical rates, or is responsiveness lagging?

themes_detail.label: Illegal Dumping Accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Illegal dumping complaints rose to 22 LAST WEEK, up 96% from an 11.2-complaint weekly baseline (z-score: 2.61), suggesting inadequate sanitation monitoring or a new waste disposal problem in the district.
evidence: 22 illegal dumping complaints LAST WEEK vs. 11.2 weekly average baseline (96% increase, z-score: 2.61)
Sustained spike (not a one-day event) suggests systemic issue rather than isolated incident
Overlaps with seasonal patterns (winter) but magnitude exceeds historical variation
reporting_angles: Site mapping: Cluster 311 complaints to identify dumping hotspots—waterfront, underdeveloped lots, near commercial areas?
DSNY enforcement: How often are dump sites cleaned? Are repeat locations being monitored?
Source investigation: Are complaints tied to construction debris, residential waste, or industrial dumping? Any pattern by type?

themes_detail.label: Elevator System Failures (Earlier Spike)
themes_detail.summary: Elevator complaints spiked to 12 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 405% jump from 2.4 complaints weekly (z-score: 4.55), pointing to either a widespread system failure in aging buildings or a surge in non-functional units affecting residents' accessibility.
evidence: 12 elevator complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 2.4 weekly average (405% increase, z-score: 4.55)
Spike appears to have peaked 2 weeks ago—current status unclear; may have resolved or shifted to other complaint categories
Suggests building-specific or weather-related failure event rather than gradual deterioration
reporting_angles: DOB records: Which buildings generated elevator complaints? Pull inspection histories and violation records.
Building conditions: Visit buildings with multiple complaints—are they public housing, private rental, owner-occupied? What's repair timeline?
Accessibility impact: Interview elderly and disabled residents about how outages affect their daily life.
Maintenance trend: Is this part of broader aging-infrastructure crisis in Flatlands/Canarsie?
